import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
customer_segments = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Select relevant columns
segments = ['Graduation', 'Secondary', 'Primary', 'Unknown', 'Tertiary']
data = customer_segments.groupby('Education')['Response'].value_counts().unstack().fillna(0)

# Create a stacked bar chart
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.set_style('whitegrid')
sns.barplot(data=data, x=data.columns, y=data.index, hue=segments, edgecolor='black', ci='sd', capsize=.2, errwidth=0.5)
plt.xlabel('Education')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.title('Customer Response by Education Level')
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
customer_segments = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Select relevant columns
segments = ['Graduation', 'Secondary', 'Primary', 'Unknown', 'Tertiary']
data = customer_segments.groupby('Education')['Response'].value_counts().unstack().fillna(0)

# Create a stacked bar chart
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.set_style('whitegrid')
sns.barplot(data=data, x=data.columns, y=data.index, hue=segments, edgecolor='black', ci='sd', capsize=.2, errwidth=0.5)
plt.xlabel('Education')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.title('Customer Response by Education Level')
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
